answer: A new head needs a fresh machine and a fresh violet seal, burned into silicon that can never be sealed again. The violet keeps a horizon listing every seal it minted for that maker, and it signs a new one only after reading that horizon end to end, charging one ivory for each seal it reads. The first head of an honest maker costs one ivory and one machine; a maker's thousandth costs a thousand tusks of ivory and a thousand machines, minted in sequence, each seal naming the one before. The chain hangs off the maker's own root, so no fresh wallet starts over.
